extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, educators, and scholars interested in Marjane Satrapi's Persepolis and graphic memoirs
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative criteria and standards the article uses to describe, classify, teach, criticize, or adapt Marjane Satrapi's Persepolis (the autobiographical graphic novel series).

rubrics_metrics.name: Autobiographical/memoir status
rubrics_metrics.description: Persepolis is presented and evaluated as an autobiographical graphic novel / illustrated memoir that depicts the author's childhood and early adult years in Iran and Austria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page emphasizes that the work is a memoir and Bildungsroman — the autobiographical nature shapes expectations for truthfulness, witness, and personal perspective rather than fictional invention. Evaluation should consider fidelity to personal experience and memoir conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of visual literacy and black-and-white art
rubrics_metrics.description: Satrapi wrote Persepolis in a black-and-white format and uses images that can be 'read' (visual literacy) to enhance the message of the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques and analysis highlight the heavy black-and-white drawings that darken dialogue and the belief that pictures can be read like language; assessors should consider how the visual style conveys tone, theme, and narrative meaning (e.g., visual simplicity drawing attention to political events).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative viewpoint and child's perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Telling the story from a child's point of view affords 'supreme authenticity and immediacy', making events accessible and emotionally immediate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating effectiveness, consider how the child's POV shapes tone, reliability, accessibility, and pedagogical suitability; assess the degree to which a juvenile narrator produces authenticity and empathetic engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme of 'witnessing' and precarity of survival
rubrics_metrics.description: A central evaluative dimension is Persepolis's emphasis on 'witnessing' — describing life from the viewpoint of someone observing political/social chaos — and on the precarity of survival under repression and war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics assess how well the work conveys witnessing and precarity: look for moments that translate complex historical/political events into personal, relatable experiences and for narrative/visual strategies that communicate vulnerability and survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feminist themes and portrayal of women/the veil
rubrics_metrics.description: The memoir contains feminist themes, using the veil as a metaphor for control and exploring women’s agency and oppression under the Islamic state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should examine representations of gender, how the veil is deployed symbolically, nuanced portrayals that challenge Western stereotypes, and whether the work advances feminist critique or alternative readings (e.g., veil as complex symbol, not solely oppression).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre classification: 'graphic novel' vs 'graphic narrative'
rubrics_metrics.description: There is debate over labeling Persepolis as a 'graphic novel' (a term often associated with fiction) versus a 'graphic narrative' for its non-fiction, autobiographical character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying or cataloguing the work, consider criteria such as fiction vs non-fiction, storytelling focus, and the unique narrative qualities of autobiographical comics; shelving or labeling decisions should reflect these distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical value and classroom suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Persepolis is evaluated as a teaching tool that 'lends itself to discussion of literary strategies' and aids development of visual literacy, critical thinking, and broader discussions of cultural difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educators assessing suitability should weigh its capacity to disrupt one-dimensional images of Iran, foster critical discussion, and develop literacy skills; also consider appropriate grade level and curricular goals when assigning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content appropriateness and grounds for challenge/censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: The book has been challenged and removed in some school contexts due to 'graphic language and images', 'coarse language and scenes of torture', sexual content, or perceived inappropriateness for assigned age groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors and decision-makers (e.g., school boards) should identify specific content concerns (language, violence, sexual themes), consider age-appropriateness, and balance censorship claims against academic freedom and pedagogical benefit; the article documents cases and ALA challenge rankings as context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cultural representation and humanization
rubrics_metrics.description: A key evaluative claim is that Persepolis humanizes Iran, connects Western and Iranian worlds, and serves as a cross-cultural form of representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should look at how effectively the work humanizes its subjects, counters stereotypes, and facilitates cross-cultural understanding, including whether it presents counter-historical narratives unfamiliar to Western readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylistic and artistic influences
rubrics_metrics.description: The page notes influences (e.g., German expressionism) and Satrapi's artistic choices in combining text and drawings to represent culture and history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique should consider lineage and influences, how artistic choices (composition, expressionist elements, paneling) support themes, and whether the visual rhetoric effectively conveys historical/cultural contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reception, impact, and adaptation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Persepolis's success is evaluated by sales (over 2 million), translations, critical reception (Time, Newsweek, awards), inclusion on 'best books' lists, and adaptation into an award-winning animated film (festival prizes, Academy Award nomination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative (sales, translations, awards) and qualitative (reviews, cultural impact, pedagogy) measures to gauge the work's influence and success; recognition and adaptations are treated as evidence of significance.
